features.name: is_prime_working_age
features.description: Boolean indicator for individuals in their prime working years (25 to 55).
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a clear threshold for tree models to split on a key demographic segment, reducing the need for multiple age-based splits.

features.name: net_capital_change
features.description: The net difference between capital gains and capital losses.
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows the model to directly split on net capital accumulation, capturing overall financial investment status in a single feature.

features.name: hours_per_week_category
features.description: Ordinal categorization of working hours: part-time (0), standard full-time (1), overtime (2), and extreme overtime (3).
features.expected_model_benefit: Groups working hours into standard ordinal buckets, allowing tree models to make semantic splits on employment type rather than continuous hours.

features.name: education_hours_interaction
features.description: Nonlinear interaction between years of education and hours worked per week.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the combined effect of human capital and labor input, highlighting individuals with both high education and high work commitment.

features.name: has_capital_anomaly
features.description: Boolean indicator for the presence of any capital market participation (either gains or losses).
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a direct boolean split for financial activity, which is often a strong differentiator in economic datasets.

features.name: age_education_ratio
features.description: Ratio of age to years of education, indicating the relative time spent in the workforce versus in school.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a continuous ratio that helps identify individuals who may have delayed their education or advanced quickly, offering a unique splitting criterion.

features.name: log_fnlwgt
features.description: Logarithmic transformation of the final weight variable.
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses the large range of the final weight variable, reducing the impact of extreme outliers and creating a smoother distribution for tree splits.

features.name: work_intensity_metric
features.description: A nonlinear metric combining the square root of hours worked and the logarithm of age.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a continuous feature that scales work hours by age, helping the model identify patterns of intense labor participation across different life stages.

features.name: career_stage_index
features.description: Semantic assessment of the individual's career stage based on their age, education level, and hours worked per week, ranging from early career (low score) to late career/retirement (high score).
features.expected_model_benefit: Offers a semantic grouping of individuals into career stages, allowing tree models to make broader demographic splits before fine-tuning with continuous variables.

features.name: financial_stability_score
features.description: An estimated score representing financial stability derived from capital gains, capital losses, and consistent working hours.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a holistic assessment of financial health, giving the model a high-level feature to separate individuals with stable versus unstable economic situations.

features.name: occupational_skill_requirement
features.description: A semantic judgment of the skill level typically required for the individual's occupation and education combination.
features.expected_model_benefit: Translates categorical occupation and education codes into an ordinal skill metric, which tree models can split on more effectively than high-cardinality nominal variables.

features.name: family_responsibility_index
features.description: An index evaluating the level of family responsibility based on marital status, relationship role, and age.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines multiple relationship and marital status categories into a single ordinal index, simplifying the tree's ability to split on household structure.
